project18_forced_cut_review.kind: independent mathematical inspection, not an official feasibility proof
reviewed_steps: Selected identities are strict ancestors of A and have a direct consumer strictly after B, so they remain live throughout the forced interval.
Latest identity copies occupy distinct result positions, making their next-instruction ages distinct integers from 1 through W.
The sum of k ages varies within a range of width k*(W-k).
Each forced intervening original instruction raises the sum by k; each selected COPY changes it by k-d, at least -(W-k).
The resulting necessary COPY bound is max(0, ceil(k*L/(W-k)-k)); overlapping certificates are combined by maximum, never sum.
project18_forced_cut_review.assumptions: Original instructions execute once, distinct original identity is preserved, only COPY is inserted, k<W, pure uniquely named and disjoint GET/SET registers, no original COPY, recomputation, reread, spill or value aliasing.
project18_forced_cut_review.limitation: The full 336 corpus includes identity-model infeasible cases. Its aggregate necessary bound does not establish the official valid-block distribution or Level1 failure. Successful-subset bounds are not achieved ratios.
